findings.summary: SOL2-1 is still only partly fixed for H3. The append check tests only the first character after the '- ' or '  ' prefix, so a heading, a table, a block quote, a fenced code block or an HTML heading can still be appended inside a bullet. README lines 39-41 ('no heading, table, quote or code block can be added') and REVIEW_BRIEF line 16 ('inside a bullet or not') claim more than the model enforces.

findings.summary: The text never says how the decided cleanup can keep one unit from removing another unit's socket. O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT (and O-T04-HS53, line 254) requires both that systemd's RuntimeDirectory= cleanup clears a stale I01 path and that no unit's stop or restart removes another listener's live socket. For the second it says only that 'the units' configuration must' hold it. No configuration is named, and nothing says what follows if T04 finds that none exists. By the reviewer's reading of systemd, plain RuntimeDirectory= in each of the three units cannot meet both requirements.
findings.evidence: README lines 100-104 and the obligation correctly say the shared directory /run/planeon/live-proxy/ holds I01, I02 and I05 (base §3). They also say that under matrix v6's grant only unit configuration, not the matrix, protects the other sockets, and that systemd's shared-directory behaviour is a T04 question. The following is the reviewer's reading of systemd.exec(5) and could not be checked here: the research tree has no systemd source or manual, and no network was used. RuntimeDirectory= removal is per unit and not reference-counted. With the default RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=no, stopping or restarting any unit that lists planeon/live-proxy removes the whole innermost directory. Under matrix v6, init_t may unlink all four planeon socket types, so this now also removes the broker's and the gate's live sockets. Matrix v5 gives init_t no getattr or unlink on any of them, which was verified with selinux_matrix_v3.allowed. With RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes or restart, the stale I01 path survives those stops, and the observer's next bind fails because it never unlinks. If this reading holds, the two outcomes conflict whenever the cleanup is 'systemd's standard RuntimeDirectory= cleanup', and only a per-socket removal beyond it meets both. SOL-SYSTEMD-CLEANS names RuntimeDirectory= specifically, so this may need the owner's word. Fix: state the conflict next to the T04 question, and record the consequence if T04 confirms it: O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT cannot be met by RuntimeDirectory= alone, and the cleanup mechanism goes back to the owner. Alternatively, name a configuration that meets both.

findings.summary: Two statements depend on the I01 socket file actually being labelled planeon_observer_sock_t: H1's 'which socket files the observer may create (planeon_observer_sock_t)', and the systemd-cleans route through v6's per-type grant. That label comes only from a named type transition that W03 adds, and T04 does not check it. This is SOL2-4 (a), which candidate 3's disposition does not answer.
findings.evidence: Matrix v5 has four typeTransitions: planeon (dir), sealed, effect-admission.sock and policy-write.sock. None covers policy-observer.sock. allowed() gives planeon_observer_t sock_file create True on planeon_observer_sock_t, False on planeon_run_t and on the other planeon socket types, and None (outside the matrix) on undeclared types such as tmp_t and var_run_t. An abstract-namespace AF_UNIX name creates no socket file. This is the reviewer's reading, since net/unix is not in the research tree. A missing rule fails closed at bind, because the observer has no sock_file create on planeon_run_t, so this is advice only. Suggest that O-T04-HS53 confirm the I01 socket file carries planeon_observer_sock_t, and that H1 say the limit covers the matrix's declared types plus W03's rule, with connectto (server only) as the bound that always holds.

listen and bind: <research>/net/socket.c:1883-1895 (__sys_listen_socket) calls only security_socket_listen; security_socket_bind is at :1840 in __sys_bind_socket. O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP, O-T04-HS53 (listen without bind, port 0, inside the range, on AF_INET and AF_INET6) and O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP close it, because every listen path reaches security_socket_listen.
